evidence_text: The Computer History Museum records that Apple II debuted on April 16, 1977 at the first West Coast Computer Faire and was a hit.
decision: Introduce a fully assembled personal computer to a new general audience.
actual_change: Apple debuted the Apple II at the first West Coast Computer Faire.
before_state: Apple was a newly founded personal-computer company.
after_state: Apple had introduced its first mass-market product.
trigger: Demand for accessible personal computing beyond hobbyists.
outcome: The Apple II became Apple’s first mass-market computer.

evidence_text: Microsoft's official history records the April 7, 1975 headline: Altair BASIC is ready and working.
decision: Ship working BASIC software for the Altair microcomputer.
actual_change: Microsoft released working Altair BASIC.
before_state: A new software venture pursuing microcomputer users.
after_state: A working product was available for early microcomputer users.
trigger: Emergence of the Altair microcomputer.
outcome: Altair BASIC established Microsoft's first product launch.

evidence_text: Microsoft records that IBM introduced its PC with Microsoft's 16-bit operating system, MS-DOS 1.0, on August 12, 1981.
decision: Distribute an operating system through the IBM PC platform.
actual_change: IBM introduced its PC with Microsoft MS-DOS 1.0.
before_state: Microsoft sold microcomputer software products.
after_state: Microsoft entered the operating-system business through the IBM PC platform.
trigger: IBM personal-computer launch.
outcome: MS-DOS established a major operating-system distribution channel.

evidence_text: Microsoft announced retail shipment of Microsoft Windows on November 20, 1985.
decision: Launch Microsoft Windows as a graphical operating environment.
actual_change: Microsoft shipped Windows to retail dealers and distributors.
before_state: Microsoft's operating-system offering centered on MS-DOS.
after_state: Microsoft added a graphical operating environment to its product line.
trigger: Need for easier personal-computer interaction.
outcome: Windows began its commercial product lifecycle.

source_title: Here’s How a Four-Page Contract Started The Walt Disney Company
evidence_text: The Walt Disney Company states it officially began on October 16, 1923 when Walt Disney signed a contract to produce and distribute the Alice Comedies.
decision: Secure a distribution contract for the Alice Comedies.
actual_change: Walt Disney signed the contract to produce and distribute the Alice Comedies.
before_state: Walt Disney had moved to Hollywood after earlier studios failed.
after_state: The new studio had a distributor and a first production commitment.
trigger: A distributor needed new animated content.
outcome: The contract established the studio that became The Walt Disney Company.

evidence_text: Ford records that the first car built by Ford Motor Company was sold on July 15, 1903.
decision: Sell the first car built by the company.
actual_change: Ford Motor Company sold its first car.
before_state: Ford Motor Company had just been created.
after_state: Ford had completed its first vehicle sale.
trigger: Initial automobile production.
outcome: The company converted its first manufactured car into a customer sale.

source_title: A Step Into The Future: GE Turns 130
evidence_text: GE records that Edison Electric Company merged with Thomson & Houston to form General Electric on April 15, 1892.
decision: Combine Edison Electric and Thomson & Houston into General Electric.
actual_change: Edison Electric Company merged with Thomson & Houston to form General Electric.
before_state: Two separate electrical companies.
after_state: A combined General Electric Company.
trigger: Strategic merger of electrical businesses.
outcome: General Electric was formed.

evidence_text: Walmart records that Sam Walton opened the first Walmart store in Rogers, Arkansas on July 2, 1962.
decision: Open the first Walmart discount store.
actual_change: Sam Walton opened the first Walmart store in Rogers, Arkansas.
before_state: Sam Walton’s prior retail operations.
after_state: A new Walmart discount-store format was operating.
trigger: Low-price retail strategy.
outcome: Walmart began operating its first store.

evidence_text: ExxonMobil records that Exxon and Mobil joined to form Exxon Mobil Corporation on November 30, 1999.
decision: Combine Exxon and Mobil into Exxon Mobil Corporation.
actual_change: Exxon and Mobil joined to form Exxon Mobil Corporation.
before_state: Exxon and Mobil operated as separate large energy companies.
after_state: A combined Exxon Mobil Corporation operated as an integrated energy company.
trigger: Need to strengthen global competitiveness in a more competitive energy industry.
outcome: Exxon Mobil Corporation was formed.

source_title: First Online DVD Rental Store Opens
evidence_text: Netflix announced opening world’s first Internet store to offer DVD rentals on April 14, 1998.
decision: Open online store for DVD rental and purchase.
actual_change: Netflix opened Internet store offering DVD rentals and purchases.
before_state: DVD rental depended on physical retail stores.
after_state: Customers could rent or buy DVDs online with delivery.
trigger: Need for wider DVD selection and online convenience.
outcome: Netflix created online DVD-rental retail category.

source_title: Tesla Motors Begins Regular Production of 2008 Tesla Roadster
evidence_text: Tesla states regular production of the 2008 Tesla Roadster commenced on March 17, 2008.
decision: Begin regular production of Tesla Roadster.
actual_change: Tesla commenced regular production of the 2008 Roadster.
before_state: Tesla had a Roadster prototype and reservations.
after_state: Tesla had begun regular production of a production electric vehicle.
trigger: Validated demand and completed regulatory approvals.
outcome: Tesla converted Roadster concept into production vehicle.

evidence_text: Amazon states it went public on May 15, 1997.
decision: Complete initial public offering.
actual_change: Amazon went public at an IPO price of $18.00.
before_state: Amazon operated as a private online retailer.
after_state: Amazon had public-market financing and listed common stock.
trigger: Need capital to support growth of online retail operations.
outcome: Amazon completed its initial public offering.

evidence_text: Ford records first Model T shipment to a customer on October 1, 1908.
decision: Ship first Model T to customer.
actual_change: Ford shipped Model T to its first customer.
before_state: Ford sold earlier automobile models.
after_state: Ford had launched a durable, affordable Model T to customers.
trigger: Goal to create affordable, simple, durable vehicle.
outcome: Model T became Ford’s mass-market automobile.

source_title: Mickey Mouse to Celebrate His Birthday with a Trip Around the World
evidence_text: Disney records Steamboat Willie’s theatrical release at Colony Theatre on November 18, 1928.
decision: Release Steamboat Willie theatrically.
actual_change: Disney released Steamboat Willie, Mickey’s first theatrical film.
before_state: Disney studio produced animated films before Mickey’s first theatrical release.
after_state: Mickey’s sound-animation film reached theatrical audiences.
trigger: Need to differentiate animated entertainment with synchronized sound.
outcome: Mickey became Disney’s enduring global ambassador.

evidence_text: Pfizer records that 240,000 shares of new common stock were offered to public on June 22, 1942.
decision: Offer new common stock to public.
actual_change: Pfizer offered 240,000 shares of new common stock publicly.
before_state: Pfizer was privately held.
after_state: Pfizer had public shareholders.
trigger: Need capital for pharmaceutical growth.
outcome: Pfizer became publicly held.

evidence_text: Pfizer records FDA approval of Terramycin on March 15, 1950.
decision: Launch Terramycin under Pfizer label after FDA approval.
actual_change: Pfizer introduced Terramycin as its first pharmaceutical sold in United States under Pfizer label.
before_state: Pfizer had manufacturing and fermentation capabilities.
after_state: Pfizer had first proprietary branded pharmaceutical product and sales force.
trigger: FDA approval of Terramycin.
outcome: Terramycin established Pfizer-branded pharmaceutical selling.

evidence_text: Walmart records offering 300,000 common shares to public on October 1, 1970.
decision: Offer common shares to public.
actual_change: Walmart offered 300,000 shares at $16.50 per share.
before_state: Walmart was privately financed discount retailer.
after_state: Walmart had public shareholders and growth capital.
trigger: Need capital to expand discount-store network.
outcome: Walmart became publicly traded.

source_title: Visa Inc. Prices Initial Public Offering
evidence_text: Visa records its shares beginning NYSE trading on March 19, 2008 after initial public offering.
decision: List Visa shares on New York Stock Exchange.
actual_change: Visa shares began NYSE trading under ticker V.
before_state: Visa had completed global reorganization.
after_state: Visa operated as publicly traded company.
trigger: Global reorganization and public capital strategy.
outcome: Visa became public company.

evidence_text: Apple records initial public offering on December 12, 1980.
decision: Complete Apple initial public offering.
actual_change: Apple went public at $22 per share.
before_state: Apple was private personal-computer company.
after_state: Apple had public shareholders and growth capital.
trigger: Need capital to expand personal-computer business.
outcome: Apple completed initial public offering.

evidence_text: Microsoft records initial public offering on March 13, 1986.
decision: Complete Microsoft initial public offering.
actual_change: Microsoft went public at $21 per share.
before_state: Microsoft was private software company.
after_state: Microsoft had public shareholders and growth capital.
trigger: Need capital to expand software business.
outcome: Microsoft completed initial public offering.

evidence_text: American Tower records Class A common stock commenced NYSE trading on June 5, 1998 after separation from American Radio.
decision: Begin NYSE trading as independent American Tower.
actual_change: American Tower Class A stock commenced NYSE trading after separation from American Radio.
before_state: American Tower operated as part of American Radio Systems.
after_state: American Tower operated as independent publicly traded company.
trigger: Corporate separation after parent merger.
outcome: American Tower became independent public communications-infrastructure company.
